A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSD-SR research and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Matching the relocated references and supplementary material supports a complete comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original super-resolution benchmark results, component ablations, timing measurements, qualitative comparisons, and a 50-participant user study.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds comparisons using matching base models, DASM parameter experiments, and an additional appendix preference result.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 changes the reconstruction objective from LPIPS alone to weighted LPIPS plus latent MSE, with an increasing LPIPS weight. Section 4.1 describes initial training without DASM, followed by removing MSE and enabling DASM. These revise training within the retained TSD/TSM/DASM framework; the one-step inference procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DIV2K, Flickr2K, LSDIR, and the first 10,000 FFHQ faces, and evaluate on DIV2K-Val, RealSR, and DRealSR. The added backbone and parameter experiments retain this Real-ISR coverage; no additional dataset, image domain, or task requirement is identified.

E2.justification: The named single-step, multi-step, GAN, and Figure 13 comparator sets are retained. New Table 5 reuses AddSR and OSEDiff with matching TSD-SR base models. Updated OSEDiff scores do not establish a changed comparison method, and the additional appendix preference statement identifies no new comparator.

E3.justification: V3 adds SD2-base and SD2.1-base controlled comparisons and a DASM parameter grid covering N=2,4,8 and s=25,50,100 (Tables 5–6). Table 4 also replaces NIQE with LPIPS, DISTS, and FID while retaining MUSIQ, MANIQA, and CLIPIQA. Together these substantially expand controlled evaluation and revise the component-ablation assessment.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained TSM/DASM removal experiments, v3 tests whether advantages persist with matching base models and investigates sensitivity to DASM iteration count and step size. It expands component-ablation evidence to perceptual and distribution metrics. Appendix C also adds a quantified preference result supporting the existing PSNR/SSIM critique, although its protocol is unspecified.

E5.justification: Figure 5 retains its mean and standard-deviation display. Neither version supplies benchmark run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice. The additional preference percentage is a result rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: TSD-SR results change throughout the benchmark tables: DRealSR PSNR changes from 26.01 to 27.77, while DIV2K-Val FID changes from 23.55 to 29.16. OSEDiff's DRealSR LPIPS changes from 0.3177 to 0.2968. Rankings also change, including OSEDiff overtaking TSD-SR on DIV2K-Val FID. Revised training prevents interpreting these as controlled version-to-version gains. V3 additionally reports Tables 5–6 and a separate 90.28% preference result; the original 69.2% study remains.

T1.justification: Equations 7–8 revise the formal training-objective definition by adding latent MSE and separate loss weights. The TSM derivation in Appendix D, including Equations 10–12 and the control-variate argument, remains unchanged. The added Sticking the Landing citation supplies attribution rather than a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: one-step Real-ISR through TSD and DASM, improved realism and detail recovery, and fast inference. Their broad performance and speed claims remain substantively unchanged; the added experiments provide supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendices A/C refine the metric discussion toward PSNR/SSIM limitations arising from spatial misalignment and distribution-based restoration. V3 also explains initial MSE stabilization versus later oversmoothing and interprets DASM parameter choices through regularization and training cost. The model-size limitation and proposed compression work remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 supplies loss-weight and training-stage details, specifies DASM defaults N=4 and s=50, changes reported training time from roughly 48 to 96 hours, and adds a prospective code-release address. Hardware, batch size, learning rates, LoRA rank, and guidance weight are retained. Appendix Algorithm 1 still omits the newly described training stages and weighting schedule.

R1.justification: V3 adds Roeder et al.'s Sticking the Landing reference to the existing control-variate discussion and explicitly attributes the student fine-tuning arrangement to OSEDiff. The related-work categories and positioning relative to GAN, multi-step diffusion, and one-step diffusion methods otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 locally rewrites experimental and metric discussions, expands the ablation narrative, and revises Appendices A/C. It adds a supplementary overview, acknowledgments, and an author affiliation, and moves the references behind the appendix prose. Most introductory and methodological language and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 5–6 and changes Table 4's metric columns. Existing tables and figures are repositioned or resized, and references share pages with supplementary figures and Algorithm 1. The thirteen figures retain their visual evidence, and the overall two-column presentation remains.

improvement.justification: Table 5 strengthens attribution by comparing TSD-SR with AddSR and OSEDiff using matching base models, while Table 6 and the disclosed defaults improve experimental support and reproducibility. These are meaningful but limited gains: the additional 90.28% preference result lacks its own protocol, and Algorithm 1 does not incorporate the revised training description. Changed benchmark scores alone do not establish improved paper quality.
